editorial_thesis: The newest practical edge is not more autonomous action; it is making agent context, design intent, browser capabilities, and evidence boundaries explicit enough to review.

topic_groups.title: Design-to-Delivery Context
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A coverage gap with direct Buildn/client leverage: Figma is turning design systems and code context into agent-readable production infrastructure, materially extending the older design-to-production theme.

sources.title: Build by Design: New Workflows for New Ways of Building
sources.why_selected: Figma connects code layers, design-system guidelines, code sources, and shared context on one canvas.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a visual review packet that keeps intent, implementation, and decisions together.

sources.title: How to Lighten Design System Upkeep With the Figma Agent
sources.why_selected: The agent audits drift, documents components, and packages recurring checks as skills.
sources.usefulness: Turn design-system hygiene into a repeatable client delivery offer.

sources.title: Workflow Lab: Staying in the Flow with Figma’s Agent
sources.why_selected: It shows a useful human/agent split: automate repair and synthesis, reserve judgment for ambiguity and policy.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the checkpoint pattern for Buildn reviewable delegated work.

topic_groups.title: Agent-Aware Browser Tooling
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh developer-tool signal: Chrome DevTools is shipping explicit controls for agent plugins, JavaScript execution, file roots, source maps, and reproducible performance—an actionable complement to recent runtime-boundary coverage.

sources.title: New in DevTools — October 2026
sources.why_selected: The DevTools MCP surface now exposes concrete capability controls and inspection primitives.
sources.usefulness: Test least-privilege browser agents against a real, documented control surface.

sources.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents
sources.why_selected: PrefDiag-Bench shows that selecting evidence and recognizing when a preference activates are harder than final task completion.
sources.usefulness: Add preference evidence and trigger timing to agent acceptance tests.

sources.title: ASPIRE: Agentic Safety & Prompt Injection Red-teaming Engine
sources.why_selected: ASPIRE models injection as an influence path from untrusted content to privileged side effects, not as a bad string.
sources.usefulness: Use path coverage to threat-model browser and document agents.

topic_groups.title: Professional Stateful Memory
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A material update rather than a repeat of yesterday’s deletion theme: new benchmarks move memory evaluation from personal recall to evolving visual artifacts, authority changes, and professional evidence reconciliation.

sources.title: DSV-Mem: Evaluating Multimodal Memory in Professional Workflows
sources.why_selected: The strongest tested baseline reaches only 39.6% on dense, stateful visual workflows against an 81.8% human baseline.
sources.usefulness: Design evidence ledgers for dashboards, designs, incident records, and client artifacts.

sources.title: DyadMem: A Long-Term Memory Benchmark of How Agents Work with Users
sources.why_selected: It separates user facts, agent methods, agent identity, knowledge, and episodes across capture, update, recall, and QA.
sources.usefulness: Use its memory taxonomy to prevent personal context and reusable workflow knowledge from collapsing together.

sources.title: MeMoREval: Memory Modality for Embodied Agents
sources.why_selected: It measures retained evidence modality and read/write cost separately, showing frames plus scene graphs can outperform text-only summaries.
sources.usefulness: Choose memory formats by task and cost instead of defaulting to prose summaries.
